correctness.rationale: The online rule sends an item eligible to pair e={u,v} to the endpoint with smaller pair-specific cumulative load (singletons forced). Induction gives -B_{v,e}<=Q_{u,e}-Q_{v,e}<=B_{u,e} after EVERY arrival even with arbitrary positive real weights. For any agent i, exact identity L_i-P_i=1/2 sum_{e incident i}(Q_{i,e}-Q_{other,e}). At most 2 DISTINCT partner pairs implies simultaneous -b_i^-<=L_i-P_i<=b_i^+ for all prefixes, good and chore versions, regardless of repeated edges or horizon. Adaptive knockout on eight agents with seven unit pair-jobs forms a degree-3 tree and forces winner load3, proportional share3/2, failure after removing one unit. The inspected verifier checks integer finite examples; induction proves all positive real weights.

value.rationale: Maximum distinct partner degree is a natural sparseness/interaction restriction in restricted-assignment scheduling. A deterministic pair-local greedy rule that simultaneously attains exact two-sided Prop1 for arbitrary weights and prefixes, together with a matching degree-3 obstruction, gives a sharp structural boundary rather than a marginal improvement in a toy instance.
